_meta.description: Game theory behavioral data — competition, cooperation, trust patterns from experimental economics
_meta.sources: Meta-analyses and laboratory experiments from peer-reviewed journals

prisoners_dilemma.description: Two players choose to cooperate or defect; mutual cooperation is optimal but defection is individually rational
prisoners_dilemma.source: Sally 1995 meta-analysis of PD experiments 1958-1995; Embrey, Frechette & Yuksel 2017

communication_allowed.note: Communication increases cooperation by ~40 percentage points
communication_allowed.source: Sally 1995 meta-analysis — communication one of few significant variables

anonymous_one_shot.source: Brosig 2002, some experimental results in PD game

decline_over_rounds.note: Cooperation declines in finitely repeated games, especially in final rounds (end-game effect)

gender_effects.note: Small but persistent gender difference favoring women

ultimatum_game.description: Proposer divides a sum; responder accepts or rejects (both get nothing if rejected)

offers.source: Camerer 2003 Behavioral Game Theory; Guth et al. 1982 original study

high_stakes.note: With stakes up to 40 weeks wages (India), rejection rates approach zero
high_stakes.source: Andersen et al. 2011, AER — high-stakes ultimatum in India

earned_entitlement.note: When proposers earn the right to propose, offers decrease and rejections decrease

public_goods_game.description: Players decide how much of endowment to contribute to a shared pool; pool is multiplied and shared equally

without_punishment.note: Contributions decline steadily to near zero without enforcement

with_punishment.note: 82.5% contribute entire endowment in final period with punishment; contributions between 50-95% of endowment maintained
with_punishment.source: Fehr & Gachter 2000, Cooperation and Punishment in Public Goods Experiments, AER

behavioral_types.note: ~50% are conditional cooperators, ~30% free-riders, rest mixed

group_size_effect.note: Cooperation decreases with group size due to increased strategic uncertainty

multiplier_effect.note: Higher marginal per-capita return increases contributions

trust_game.description: Sender sends money (tripled by experimenter) to receiver who decides how much to return
trust_game.source: Johnson & Mislin 2011 meta-analysis of 162 replications, 23,000+ participants

original_study.source: Berg, Dickhaut & McCabe 1995, Games and Economic Behavior

trustworthiness.note: ~55% return at least the amount sent (showing reciprocity)

dictator_game.description: Dictator decides how to split money; recipient has no choice (no strategic interaction)

giving_distribution.note: 36.1% give nothing, 16.7% split evenly, 63.9% give something

double_blind.note: Giving drops when anonymity is maximized

earned_money.note: Giving drops further when dictator earned the money

deserving_recipient.note: Giving increases when recipient is seen as deserving (e.g., charity)

tragedy_of_commons.description: Shared resource depleted by self-interested actors; classic collective action problem
tragedy_of_commons.note: Groups typically extract 140% of socially optimal level (40% over-extraction)

without_communication.note: Without communication, extraction converges near Nash equilibrium (~150% of optimal)
without_communication.source: Ostrom, Gardner & Walker 1994, Rules Games and Common-Pool Resources

sustainability_factors.note: 45% of assortatively matched rule-following groups preserve resource for entire experiment
sustainability_factors.source: Cambridge review of CPR game experiments

resource_growth_effect.note: Higher resource regeneration rate makes sustainable management more likely
resource_growth_effect.source: ScienceDirect, social and ecological determinants of CPR sustainability

auction_behavior.description: Bidding in common-value auctions where the item has the same value for all bidders

winners_curse.note: At least 47% of all bids attributed to winner's curse (overbidding)
winners_curse.source: Kagel & Levin 2002, Common Value Auctions; PMC2841440
winners_curse.persistence: Persists through all 50 rounds even with experience

vs_computer_opponents.note: Significantly reduced when bidding against computers — social competition drives overbidding
vs_computer_opponents.source: PMC2841440, value of victory: social origins of winner's curse

revenue_vs_theory.note: Revenue exceeds risk-neutral Nash equilibrium predictions by ~10%

number_of_bidders_effect.note: Winner's curse severity increases with number of bidders

negotiation.description: Bargaining outcomes influenced by anchoring, first offers, and framing

first_offer_advantage.note: First offers explain ~50% of variance in final agreement price
first_offer_advantage.source: Galinsky & Mussweiler 2001, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

anchoring_effect.note: Random number (10 vs 65) shifted estimates by 20 percentage points

ambitious_first_offers.note: More ambitious first offers produce ~15% more favorable outcomes

precise_offers.note: Highly precise offers ($5,015 vs $5,000) lead recipients to make smaller counteroffers
precise_offers.source: Mason et al. 2013, Journal of Experimental Social Psychology

range_anchoring.note: Bolstering ranges spanning 5-20% above base figure produced superior outcomes for sellers
range_anchoring.source: Harvard PON, 5 experiments on range anchoring

concession_patterns.note: Parties typically make ~4 concessions; first concession is largest (~40% of total movement)
concession_patterns.source: Pruitt 1981; Thompson 2005, The Mind and Heart of the Negotiator

deadline_effect.note: ~50% of agreements reached in the last 5% of available time

competition_vs_cooperation.description: When teams outperform individuals, and when competition helps vs hurts

social_facilitation.note: Both cooperation and competition improve performance vs working alone by ~15%
social_facilitation.source: ScienceDirect 2024, cooperation and competition same benefits different costs

means_interdependent_tasks.note: Cooperative rewards increase performance on tasks requiring coordination
means_interdependent_tasks.source: Beersma et al. 2003, Academy of Management Journal

means_independent_tasks.note: Competitive rewards increase performance on independent tasks

intergroup_competition.note: External competition increases internal cooperation by ~25%
intergroup_competition.source: Bornstein 2003, Intergroup conflict; Erev et al. 1993

brainstorming.note: Nominal groups (individuals pooled) produce ~30% more ideas than interacting groups
brainstorming.source: Diehl & Stroebe 1987, JPSP; Mullen et al. 1991 meta-analysis

social_loafing.note: Individual effort decreases ~20% in groups without accountability
social_loafing.source: Karau & Williams 1993, meta-analysis of 78 studies, JPSP

market_competition.description: Business entry, exit, survival rates and competitive dynamics

business_survival_rates.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics 2024, Business Employment Dynamics

failure_reasons.source: CB Insights analysis of 156 startup post-mortems

pricing_competition.note: ~25% of industries experience significant price wars in any given 5-year period

market_entry_dynamics.note: ~12% new establishments enter and ~10% exit annually in US

first_mover_advantage.note: First movers capture ~10% higher market share on average; 1.2x survival rate vs later entrants

cooperation_baseline.note: Across all game types, cooperation increases with communication > reputation > punishment

fairness_norms.note: Across cultures, 20% is the threshold below which offers are frequently rejected

punishment_effectiveness.note: 60% willing to pay to punish defectors; punishment increases cooperation by ~35 percentage points
punishment_effectiveness.source: Fehr & Gachter 2002; Herrmann et al. 2008, Science

group_size_effects.note: Cooperation decreases ~3 percentage points per additional group member

cultural_variation.note: Ultimatum offers vary more by economic integration than individualism/collectivism

experience_effects.note: Experience generally moves behavior toward Nash equilibrium predictions
